verdict.rationale: Azure's own RBAC provides fine-grained access management to resources, and you can scope access per principal (e.g. VMs for one, networks for another). Managed identities and Entra app registration give an application or agent its own token-based credentials, so least-privilege credentials for an agent are a first-party capability. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of assigning scoped roles to service principals or managed identities used by agents, details on credential expiry and rotation, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Azure RBAC is an authorization system built on Azure Resource Manager that provides fine-grained access management to Azure resources.
